The findings are categorized into key themes: security, privacy, scalability, verifiability, and performance, with an emphasis on advanced methods like biometric encryption and quantum key distribution. Emerging trends, including quantum cryptography and decentralized governance, are explored as future avenues for innovation. Despite these advancements, challenges related to governance, user engagement, legal frameworks, and system interoperability persist. The paper concludes by identifying the need for further research into scalability and security improvements, as well as the seamless integration of blockchain solutions with existing electoral infrastructure to enable real-world adoption

articleTitle: Real-Time Solar Monitoring with Charging and Grid Control Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a real-time solar monitoring system with an integrated charging and smart grid control mechanism, emphasizing the novelty of grid integration into a hybrid power system. The system utilizes an ESP8266 microcontroller interfaced with voltage, current, and temperature sensors to monitor solar panel performance and environmental conditions. Data is transmitted to the IoT platform ThingSpeak for real-time display and analysis. A 12V lead-acid battery is charged via a solar charging circuit, and smart grid control is achieved through relays, enabling automatic switching between solar, battery, and grid power for uninterrupted power supply. When solar energy is sufficient, the system powers the load directly from the solar panel while charging the battery. When solar panel output is insufficient, it intelligently switches to grid power, which supplies the load and also charges the battery. If both solar and grid power are unavailable, the system seamlessly transitions to battery power. The system is implemented using an 18V solar panel, and an Arduino microcontroller is employed to manage the relay-based switching mechanism. This hybrid power system integrates real-time solar monitoring with smart grid functionality to enhance energy efficiency and reliability.

articleTitle: AEGIS: Adaptive Ensemble-based Guard for Intrusion Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: The evolving sophistication of cyber threats demands an adaptive, ensemble-based approach to Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). This paper introduces AEGIS, an advanced framework designed to enhance real-time threat detection through a multi-layered ensemble architecture. AEGIS incorporates novel features like adaptive thresholding, temporal-aware feature selection, and concept drift monitoring to maintain robust performance amidst dynamic and polymorphic attacks. With a combination of Random Forest classifiers and gradient boosting, AEGIS achieves 99.97% detection accuracy, while minimizing false positives. The system’s resilience is further fortified by adversarial testing, time-based cross-validation, and ensemble diversity management, ensuring high adaptability to evolving network behaviors. Our results demonstrate that AEGIS not only surpasses traditional IDS frameworks in detection accuracy but also introduces significant advancements in real-time anomaly detection, scalability, and computational efficiency. The proposed framework provides a pathway for the development of future-proof IDS architectures capable of defending against increasingly sophisticated threats.

articleTitle: Smart Agriculture: Leveraging ResNet50 for Precise Detection and Classification of Banana Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: Various diseases that greatly lower output and damage growers financial stability provide major difficulties for banana farming. Images of diseased (Sigatoka, Cordana, Pestalotiopsis) and healthy banana leaves comprise the dataset, taken with smartphone cameras and painstakingly annotated by a trained plant pathologist in Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Agricultural University and surrounding areas in Bangladesh. The research paper developed and tested the ResNet50 model on this dataset to classify the diseases. The model developed a general classification accuracy of 96.4%. With accuracy, recall, and F1-scores of above 94% for all classes, the classification report reveals that the model is robust in detecting the disorders. Especially, the model shown amazing accuracy in identifying healthy leaves with minimal misclassification. Given the Pestalotiopsis class has the best misclassification rate, the confusion matrix emphasizes even more the capacity of the model. This paper emphasizes the opportunities of deep learning in automating disease diagnosis by means of early detection and quick response, therefore supporting the global banana supply chain and enhancing disease management strategies.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Sleep Optimization: Enhancing SEL Interventions to Reduce Bedtime Procrastination
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with that of Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) interventions to address bedtime procrastination and promote better sleep hygiene. Bedtime procrastination, a prevalent issue among various age groups, often leads to insufficient sleep, negatively impacting overall health and well-being. By leveraging AI's adaptive capabilities and SEL's focus on emotional regulation and decision-making, we propose a comprehensive framework for smart sleep strategies. Our approach includes personalized interventions designed to foster better sleep routines, enhance self-discipline, and mitigate procrastination behaviors. The study evaluates the effectiveness of these AI-driven SEL interventions through a series of controlled experiments and surveys, demonstrating significant improvements in sleep patterns and overall sleep quality. These findings suggest that AI-enhanced SEL interventions offer a promising solution for reducing bedtime procrastination and improving sleep hygiene, contributing to better health outcomes and quality of life.

articleTitle: Stock Price Prediction Using Gradient Boosting Machine with Technical Indicators
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: This research endeavors to design a predictive model to forecast stock prices using a Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) regressor, specifically emphasizing the adjusted closing price to mitigate the autocorrelation issues intrinsic to time series data. The investigation encompasses a 12-month duration of historical stock data, integrating two technical indicators, namely Exponential Moving Averages (EMA_5 and EMA_10), to augment predictive precision. Gradient Boosting, recognized for its proficiency in managing intricate and non-linear data patterns, was employed to forecast forthcoming stock prices. Critical performance indicators, including Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and the Coefficient of Determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), played a role in evaluating model accuracy, attaining an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.99, thereby signifying an almost perfect correlation between actual and predicted prices. Beyond numerical assessments, visual examinations through scatter plots, residual plots, and prediction error distribution further elucidated the model’s efficiency. The findings reveal that the amalgamation of Gradient Boosting with Technical Indicators such as EMA_5 and EMA_10, coupled with an emphasis on the adjusted closing price, proves exceptionally effective for stock price forecasting. This methodology achieved an accuracy rate nearing 99%, illustrating its substantial promise for stock market prediction and its proficiency in alleviating autocorrelation challenges within time series datasets.

articleTitle: Prediction of IPL Player Selection from T20 formats using a Novel Data Balancing Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: Selecting players in the squad for the very popular Indian Premier League (IPL) is crucial. It is influenced by various factors, like popularity, fitness, and the players' performance in various cricket formats. This research paper focuses on creating a model to check whether an Indian player will be selected for IPL by analyzing the data from the year 2021-2023 across various T20 cricket tournaments, namely Sayed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, Irani Trophy, and Duleep Trophy. The collected data was preprocessed and consolidated into two datasets: batsmen and bowlers with unique player entries separately. The dataset was biased towards the non-ipl players. Thus, to address the issue of an imbalanced dataset, we tried various data balancing techniques and introduced a novel, problem-specific approach to balancing the dataset. All these balanced datasets were trained on a logistic regression model to predict player selection. Our results show that the problem-specific data balancing technique outperformed the state-of-the-art techniques, offering a more accurate and reliable solution for IPL player selection. This paper contributes a new data balancing strategy and provides valuable insights for improving player selection models in sports analytics.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Water Quality Monitoring System with Anomaly Detection and Predictive Maintenance Using Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: Water quality monitoring is crucial for safeguarding public health and preserving water resources. Traditional monitoring systems often lack real-time analysis capabilities and predictive maintenance features, limiting their effectiveness in promptly addressing water quality issues. This paper introduces an advanced IoT-based water quality monitoring system that leverages Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for data augmentation, predictive maintenance, and anomaly detection. The proposed system employs an ESP32 microcontroller equipped with pH, TDS, turbidity, and temperature sensors to gather water quality data. By integrating machine learning techniques, particularly GANs, our system aims to shift towards a more proactive approach. GANs not only enhance the dataset for training purposes but also improve the robustness of predictive models. This innovation allows for early detection of potential sensor failures and water quality anomalies, thereby enabling timely interventions. Moreover, the use of GANs helps in generating synthetic data that mimics real-world scenarios, further strengthening the system's predictive capabilities. This ensures that the models are well-equipped to handle diverse and unforeseen situations. Ultimately, this proactive methodology contributes to maintaining consistent water quality and preventing possible health hazards, fostering greater trust in water management systems.

articleTitle: Streamlined Machine Learning Workflow for Accurate Rice Yield Estimation Using Remote Sensing and Meteorological Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: The goal of this project is to use machine learning (ML), meteorological data, and remote sensing data to create an effective methodology for accurate rice yield estimation. The project entails creating a customized machine learning model with the aim of forecasting rice yields while accounting for the unique agricultural characteristics of the target region. The goal of the research is to determine the best approach for estimating rice yields by utilizing sophisticated data processing techniques and carefully assessing various machine learning models. By combining these strategies, crop production forecasts should become more accurate and provide insightful information for agricultural planning and management in a variety of geographical areas.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Detection of Lumpy Skin Disease in Cattle Using Deep Feature Extraction Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: Cattle are susceptible to a viral infection called lumpy skin disease (LSD), which was first discovered in Africa and is currently spreading to the Middle East, Asia, and some regions of Eastern Europe. Symptoms of the condition include fever, drooling, frequent tearing, and prominent skin nodules. PCR testing, virus isolation, and histopathology analysis can all be used to provide a diagnosis. There is now serious concern over the disease's prevalence in cattle. Because there are so many different diseases that can harm animals, prompt and accurate diagnosis is essential. The Neethling virus, which causes LSD, causes irreversible skin damage in afflicted cattle. Infertility, stunted growth, miscarriages, a decrease in milk production, and, in extreme circumstances, death can potentially result from the condition. The suggested remedy entails using VGG-16, VGG-19, and Inception-v3 frameworks for feature extraction and machine learning algorithms for disease detection. The strategy shows notable gains in feature extraction performance when tested on a dataset and contrasted with sophisticated approaches like KNN, SVM, NB, ANN, and LR.

Author Keywords: Neethling Virus: A Viral Infection in Cattle
Animal Illness Veterinary Medicine Diagnosis Machine Learning

articleTitle: Reflecting Intelligent Surface Performance Evaluation with Different Reflector Elements Operating at mmWave Frequency
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: The 6G basically will be depended on mmWave band to cater the user demand. The major drawback of mmWave communication is the signal loss. The signal will get attenuated at a very shorter range. In order to overcome this, new technique called Reflective Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have been introduced. The basic purpose of RIS is to reflect back the incident radiation in the required direction with minimum signal loss. In this work performance of RIS structure when loaded with isotropic antenna elements and dipole antenna element is carried out. The spacing between the RIS unit elements and the number RIS unit element, for dipole and isotropic elements is kept constant. The obtained results shows that the signal strength, is better when RIS is loaded with dipole antenna as unit element, than the isotropic antenna elements.

articleTitle: Predicting Sector Indices Using Machine Learning: A Comprehensive Analysis Incorporating Macroeconomic Indicators
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: The influence of macroeconomic indicators on stock market movement continues to attract attention, particularly in emerging markets, especially countries such as India. The objective of this study is to predict NIFTY 50 sectoral indices namely Automobile, Energy, Banking, IT, FMCG, Metal, and Realty using macroeconomic indicators such as exports, imports, exchange rates, GDP, interest discount rates, and inflation rates. Traditional regression models like Lasso, Linear Regression, Elastic Net, and advanced machine learning models like XGBoost, Decision Tree, and Random Forest Regressor, Support Vector Regressor have been used for the prediction. The experiments show that the Random Forest Regressor came out with the best performance, providing a lower Mean Squared Error (MSE) and the highest R-squared values in almost all the sectors, except the Realty sector. It proves that advanced machine learning techniques go beyond ordinary regression methods in capturing nonlinear relationships. This study highlights the importance of macroeconomic factors as drivers of sector-specific stock performances in emerging markets and the potential of using machine learning models to understand them.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Fostering Internal Stakeholders’ Performance in Academia
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: The study aims to examine the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in furthering the performance of internal stakeholders in the academia. It aims to explore the positive impact of leveraging AI in fostering the development of students, faculty members and admin or operational excellence. The study also exposes the challenges and the risks in AI adoption. AI’s role in the corporate world, especially in banking, insurance, health etc., is widely discussed and therefore, this study is a significant one as it is concerning the academia. Primary data was collected by conducting the survey. 205 respondents participated in the survey. The respondents were categorized into three clusters, namely, emerging, engaged and experienced based on the degree of adoption of AI. To examine the academic stakeholders’ behaviour, K-Means clustering method was employed. Multiple regression tool was used to study the perceived benefits of AI adoption in academia. Decision tree was used to develop challenges matrix and to study the interrelated associations. Sentiment analysis was leveraged to examine the AI adoption sentiments among stakeholders of the academia. The study revealed that AI has a positive influence on all the stakeholders of academia. AI assists teachers, helps students and admin team so that the learning is epibranchial and fruitful. AI should be adopted in a calibrated way after considering the AI challenges. The outcome is win-win for the academic world if AI is appropriately implemented.

articleTitle: Intelligent Hotel Recommendation System Using Dynamic Graph Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: Inherently, the framework of Inn Suggestion presents an entirely hybrid approach to making hotel recommendations. The framework encompasses content-based and collaborative filtering techniques into a single system by analyzing user behaviors, including past bookings and reviews, besides features, which are generally associated with hotels, such as location and price, to get relevant suggestions. At the heart of the framework lies the Adaptive Meta-Learning Hybrid algorithm that coordinates several machine learning techniques, like RNN, CNN, KNN, and Node2Vec. This meta-learning layer can recalculate the selection of algorithms dynamically based on performance in targeted subsets of users. The feature affords rapid adaptation to shifts in the user behavior and underlying data distributions, thus significantly enhancing both accuracy and diversity of recommendations over time. Key features include real-time updates, an intuitive user interface, and a robust feedback system. The technologies which architecture is based on including Node.js, Python, React.js, and cloud services, with which scalability and security are the essence of their execution. Introducing these methodologies with AMLH, the Brilliantly Inn Suggestion Framework aims to change the entire experience of booking hotels. Which means a more dynamic personalized experience through booking in respect of each user's needs and overall satisfaction toward travel planning.

articleTitle: Advancing Tomato Leaf Hygiene with Machine Learning for Enhanced Plant Health and Productivity
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: The implementation of a machine learning model to enhance hygiene permanence in tomato leaves has shown remarkable results, emphasizing the utility of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for early disease detection. Our model, trained on a comprehensive dataset of several thousand annotated images, effectively identifies subtle changes in leaf condition before visible symptoms manifest. The CNN architecture, which incorporates convolutional, pooling, and fully connected layers, was meticulously optimized for both accuracy and computational efficiency. Techniques such as dropout and batch normalization were employed to prevent overfitting, ensuring robust performance across various conditions. The real-time monitoring system, integrated with the CNN, facilitated continuous data input and early intervention, significantly curtailing the spread of diseases. Field trials validated the CNN's effectiveness, with performance metrics showing an accuracy of 92.5%, precision of 90.3%, recall of 89.7%, and an F1-score of 90%. These results indicate a high reliability in detecting leaf degradation, demonstrating the model's proficiency in identifying true positive cases and its ability to catch a large percentage of actual positives. The study confirms that integrating advanced machine learning techniques into agricultural practices can transform plant disease management, promoting sustainable farming by reducing reliance on chemical interventions and improving crop resilience. The CNN model’s continuous learning capability further supports its adaptability to evolving conditions, making it a valuable tool for enhancing tomato crop health and productivity.

articleTitle: Integrating SIEM with Zero Trust Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: The integration of Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems with Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) represents a significant advancement in cybersecurity, combining the real-time monitoring and analytical capabilities of SIEM with the rigorous access controls and continuous verification principles of Zero Trust. This paper explores the core principles of Zero Trust, examines the key functions and roles of SIEM systems, and outlines effective integration strategies. Through real-world case studies and the lessons learned from various implementations, the paper provides insights into how organizations can leverage this integration to enhance threat detection, streamline incident response, and improve overall security posture. The discussion also highlights best practices for aligning SIEM with Zero Trust policies, optimizing data collection, and addressing performance considerations to achieve a robust security framework.

articleTitle: SteganoWave
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: In an age where digital communication has taken precedence, the need for concealed and secure conversations has become ever-more important. Audio steganography facilitates the process of hiding secret messages in audio within a file or audio signal, thereby rendering the embedded data undetectable in the file. This work presents the idea of understanding and implementation of the principles of audio steganography and disclosing the methods of embedding and extracting secret messages on audio files. The main aim is to develop an audio steganography application, that embeds and extracts hidden messages, and tests the direct relation of perceptibility, capacity, and robust communication. Implementing simple steganographic method of least significant bit (LSB) a spread spectrum approach, phase coding, and echo hiding among other applications, we aim to build a versatile audio steganographic system. The work addresses some pervasive problems that accompany accessing an audio file steganographically, including maintaining some level of audio quality, securing the data, and interpreting the steganography in audio. The implementation of the work, has contributed to the body of literature around digital steganography by mapping out useful techniques for concealed communication. The systems approach to anomaly characterization illustrates both the practicality and feasibility of audio steganography as, and possibly the portent to communicate. Ultimately, the work carried out opens avenues for ongoing investigations in the field of research related to audio steganography.

articleTitle: IoT-Driven Aid Deployment Unmanned Surface Vehicle Harnessing YOLOv6-N and LoRa For Lifeguard and Border Patrol Assistance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an unmanned surface vehicle (USV) prototype designed to modernise search and rescue operations and significantly enhance maritime border surveillance. Offering an economical and distinctive alternative to current USVs in the market by integrating three primary functions: smart aid deployment, surveillance, and long-range communication by enabling swift and effective aid delivery. The prototype, which is equipped with a Raspberry Pi 4B, a Pi camera, and the YOLOv6-N object detection algorithm to identify individuals in distress, is integrated with a manipulator and Internet of Things (IoT) capabilities for real-time tracking via the Blynk application for aid deployment. Surveillance is supported by a V380 Pro camera, while LoRa RA-02 SX1278 technology ensures reliable long-range communication. The USV's distinctive lifebuoy-inspired, pentagon-shaped design enhances both stability and manoeuvrability due to its differential thrust system. Weighing just 15 kg, the USV can support drowning victims and transport essential aid kits. Which makes it ideal for military operations and lifeguard rescue missions, aiming to reduce response time and fatalities.

articleTitle: Integrating Big Data Analytics in Soil Quality Assessment: Techniques, Challenges, and Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: This review paper investigates the application of Big Data analytics, focusing on soil quality assessment, with an emphasis on the innovative benefits offered by modern data-driven techniques for improved soil management. With world food demands rising, the importance for real-time and exact soil quality monitoring has increased. Although still useful, traditional approaches to modeling are limited in their ability to capture the spatial and temporal variability of soil properties. Big Data analytics sits as the answer to the above by facilitating extensive and large volume data processing resulting in better, on-demand and scalable soil quality assessment. In the paper, we describe machine learning algorithms, remote sensing and geospatial analysis as key techniques to mine soil data at scales and resolutions unprecedented so far. We also critically evaluate the challenge of data integration (heterogeneity, scalability and multi-disciplinarity). These analytics are scalable for assessment and decision-making in precision agriculture, sustainable land management and environmental conservation. Thus, this paper synthesizes current research and practical implications in support of the need for Big Data analytics within soils and soil sciences to cover also future challenges. Future research directions are also highlighted, including the importance of improved data acquisition and algorithmic advances as well greater synergy between Big Data and conventional soil science practices..

articleTitle: Automated Sarcasm Detection in English Tweets Using CCNN and ELLSTM with Text and Emoji Embeddings
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: Automatic detection of sarcasm is one of the most challenging tasks in natural language processing; hence, extending it into the realm of English tweets-where sarcasm is usually conveyed by text and emojis-would add to the complexity. The paper addresses a new avenue in using a Customized Convolutional Neural Network combined (CCNN) with Extreme Learning Long Short-Term Memory (ELLSTM) for sarcasm detection in tweet data in English. Sarcasm is particularly challenging due to the scarcity of annotated corpora and the subtleties inherent in its detection, which relies mostly on context incongruity. This model will draw upon both linguistic and visual cues-text in tweets, along with accompanying emojis serving as non-verbal contextual indicators, akin to facial expressions-to improve the accuracy of detection. Emoji embeddings provide additional contextual information that has been identified as important for the detection of sarcasm. Experiments have been conducted with the CCNN-ELLSTM model using a dataset of sarcasm-annotated English tweets. Preliminary results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in achieving the best accuracy and F-score value of 97.57% and 0.9718, respectively. The effectiveness of text-emoji anchoring combos is shown in this work, which also supports the idea that automatic feature extraction might provide reliable and effective algorithms for recognizing sarcasm in English tweets.

Author Keywords: Emoji Embeddings and Natural Language Processing

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach to Data Clustering Using the K-Means Algorithm in Big Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: The large-scale, high-dimensionality of datasets poses major obstacles to effective and precise data clustering in the field of big data analytics. This work focuses on a well-known technique for dividing huge datasets into informative clusters: the K-Means algorithm. This approach to data clustering is efficient. However, because of scalability and computational complexity problems, K-Means is not as effective when managing large amounts of data. In order to reduce processing cost and improve clustering accuracy, this work provides an improved version of the K-Means algorithm that blends dimensionality reduction approaches and efficient initialization methods. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is used as a preprocessing step in the methodology to reduce the dimensionality of huge datasets. An optimized K-Means algorithm with improved centroid initialization is then applied. These changes lead to shorter iteration durations and higher-quality clusters. Comparing the results to standard K-Means, experiments on many big data benchmarks showed a 15% gain in cluster accuracy and a 25% reduction in execution time. To sum up, the incorporation of optimized initialization techniques and dimensionality reduction greatly improves the scalability and performance of K-Means in big data analytics, with useful implications for sectors that depend on effective data analysis.

articleTitle: Resource Optimisation with Application of AI and ML Augmenting Military Space Business Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: The study of this paper accentuates the rapid proliferation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies in augmenting military-space business by enhancing decision making processes by aggregating military-space business for expanding military efficiency. The contribution of this paper is twofold. First, the concept of utilization of AI / ML for gaining transformative capabilities in strategic decision making to navigate complex scenarios and anticipate future military challenges effectively is proposed. Second, to provide a framework and multi layered architecture of distributed networks with interrelated development and growth of the space economy resulting in achieving strategic autonomy by resource optimization in the military space domain for military-space business. The study aims to provide novel and valuable insights for military leaders and policymakers for a deeper understanding of AI and ML impact on modern decision making and application of modern mass surveillance for achieving superiority through military-space business. The paper concludes with unlocking the transformative power of AI and ML with resource optimization through space economy for military decision making which leads to faster and more effective decision making.

articleTitle: Load balancing promotes effective IoT-based data transfer in Snowflake Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: In networked devices, efficient data transportation is important for guaranteeing dependable and scalable Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructures. For this purpose, in the current work, a dynamic load-balancing mechanism is proposed to optimize the data transfer between Internet of Things nodes and Snowflake data storage. It may be fairly distributing the distributed data between IoT nodes, but traditional round-robin load balancing often overlooks the difference in node performance, which may lead to inefficient data transfer. A solution to this problem is a dynamic load-balancing mechanism that depends on nodes in real-time performing, hence its variation with transfer speed and latency. This system would dynamically select the most effective nodes that are to transmit the data and would ensure quicker and more dependable delivery of information. In the following simulation, round-robin and dynamic load-balancing strategies are compared using ten IoT nodes that are sending segmented data to a Snowflake server. Outcomes: These show that although the round-robin accomplishes reduced latency and faster transfer rates, the dynamic approach presents a fairer distribution of the load as well as reduces the possibility of node overloading while enhancing overall system robustness in the long term. This work adds to the future prospects of IoT load-balancing solutions, thus vividly showing how round-robin and dynamic approaches could present trade-offs between one another.

articleTitle: Predictive Machine Learning Models for Postpartum Hemorrhage Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) is a critical condition and a leading cause of maternal mortality worldwide, characterized by unpredictable onset and rapid progression. To address this challenge, our study introduces a novel approach that leverages advanced machine learning (ML) techniques to enhance the predictability of PPH risks, aiming to improve maternal healthcare outcomes. We developed and deployed a range of predictive models, including logistic regression, random forests, gradient boosting machines, and neural networks, utilizing a comprehensive dataset that integrates patient demographics, medical histories, and dynamic labor parameters. The models were rigorously tested and validated, with performance metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. The results demonstrated that deep learning models and gradient boosting machines significantly outperformed traditional methods, with neural networks achieving the highest performance metrics, including 93% accuracy and an AUC-ROC of 0.96. These models excelled in handling the complex, non-linear interactions within the data, providing superior predictions of PPH risk. Real-time data integration during labor further enhanced the models' accuracy and adaptability. The successful deployment of these models highlights their potential to improve early detection and risk assessment of PPH, facilitating better-informed clinical decisions. This approach underscores the transformative impact of advanced ML techniques on obstetric care, emphasizing the need for continuous updates and user-friendly tools to ensure effective integration into clinical practice.

articleTitle: Quantum Dots in Modern Medicine: Advancing Imaging, Diagnostics, and Drug Delivery
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: Quantum Dots (QDs) are transforming drug delivery with advanced modalities like targeted therapies, controlled release systems, and theranostics. They enable precise drug transport, reduce side effects, and allow real-time monitoring, particularly in cancer therapy. Innovations such as dendrimers and carbon nanotubes enhance their ability to deliver multiple or water-insoluble drugs, showcasing their potential in modern medicine. The adoption of Quantum Mechanics (QM) in pharmaceutical research accelerates drug discovery by enabling precise simulations of drug-receptor interactions and optimizing molecular designs. Techniques like Density Functional Theory (DFT) and machine learning integration enhance efficiency, reduce costs, and improve the safety of therapeutic candidates, driving innovation in drug development.

articleTitle: Algorithmic Approaches and its Analysis for the Detection of Deepfakes in Audio
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: Voice deepfakes pose a critical challenge in audio authentication, deceiving human listeners and automated systems. This study compares algorithmic approaches to detect voice deepfakes, aiming to enhance authentication system robustness. Evaluated models include LSTM, CNN, GBM, SVM, LCB net, Wirenet, Logistic Regression, KNN, AdaBoost, XGBoost, and CatBoost. Each algorithm’s performance in test accuracy and, where applicable, test loss across specified training epochs is assessed. Results indicate XGBoost achieves the highest accuracy at 99.3208828%, followed closely by GBM at 98.81%, CNN at 98.50%, and LSTM at 97.71%. In contrast, Logistic Regression and KNN exhibit lower accuracies of 74.92% and 80.65%, respectively. These findings underscore the effectiveness of gradient boosting and deep learning in detecting subtle voice manipulations, which are essential for advancing voice authentication security measures.

articleTitle: Digital Signature Authentication Using Deoxyribonucleic Acid Sequencing for Enhanced Online Verification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: In today’s digitally driven world, advanced security for online transactions and communications is more crucial than ever. This paper introduces a groundbreaking digital signature authentication framework leveraging Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) sequencing for enhanced cybersecurity. Departing from traditional cryptographic methods, our approach uses the unique complexity of DNA sequences to create unforgeable digital signatures. By integrating sophisticated bioinformatics algorithms with robust cryptographic techniques, we have developed an online verification system that is secure, private, user-friendly, and efficient. Designed to be adaptable and scalable, this framework suits a range of applications, from securing email communications to protecting financial transactions. Rigorous testing and evaluations have demonstrated the system’s effectiveness in preventing unauthorized access and significantly reducing security breaches. Utilizing DNA sequencing in our authentication process marks a pioneering step in biometric security, potentially transforming digital signature integrity and setting a new standard for future bio-cryptographic systems. This innovative method represents a significant advancement in online verification technologies, proving highly effective in ensuring the security and reliability of digital communications and transactions.

articleTitle: De-Styling Bias in #Climatical Tweets: A Neural Language Style Transfer Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: The spread of biased and misleading opinions on social media regarding climate change necessitates robust solutions to counteract misinformation and promote balanced discourse. In this study, we introduce the Semantic Neural Style Transfer Bias (SNLT) Framework, an AI-driven solution designed to identify and mitigate bias in climate-related tweets. Leveraging a curated dataset of climate change tweets collected from Twitter, we employ the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence transformer for feature extraction and BERT-based embeddings to capture semantic nuances. Our methodology integrates semantic clustering models to evaluate clustering performance using silhouette scores, including KMeans, Gaussian KMeans, keyNMF clustering, and an Autoencoder-based model. DistilBERT is further employed to classify tweets as biased or unbiased, while a Named Entity Recognition (NER) model trained on RobERTa transformers identifies word-level bias indicators. The fundamental basis of our framework is a transformer-based style transfer model, such as GPT-2, which adjusts the stylistic tone of biased text while preserving its semantic meaning. This approach employs a style-specific decoder to ensure grammatical accuracy and contextual relevance, producing text with a neutral tone through refined phrasing and word choice. Evaluation results demonstrate a substantial reduction in bias without compromising fluency or naturalness, validated through statistical metrics and human assessments. Additionally, Explainable AI techniques are integrated to enhance the transparency of model decisions, offering insights into bias mitigation processes. Our findings highlight the framework's efficacy in addressing climate misinformation and fostering constructive conversations on social media, underscoring its potential as a responsible AI tool for digital discourse.

articleTitle: Understanding Graph Neural Networks Models for Healthcare Fraud Detection in Insurance Claims
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: This study suggests using graph algorithms to detect healthcare fraud, a serious issue that can lead to significant financial losses and compromise patient care. Health care fraud is a representation of deceitful acts carried out by health providers, patients, or other individuals for the purpose of gaining undue financial profit from the health insurance program. It includes false billing, misrepresentation of diagnosis and procedure, and kickbacks at the expense of substantial financial loss and deterioration of patient care. Our approach models the relationships between patients, healthcare providers, physicians, and procedures as a graph to identify unusual patterns that may indicate fraud. We utilize publicly available tabular datasets, including beneficiary data and claims from inpatient stays and outpatient visits, transforming them into a graph structure to create a unified dataset. The system employs algorithmic analysis and graph construction techniques to identify significant nodes, abnormal clusters, and outliers within the healthcare network. This strategy offers a viable method for reducing healthcare fraud, enhancing the integrity of insurance systems, and ensuring that funds are appropriately allocated to legitimate medical needs. Ultimately, this study aims to decrease the rate of fraud in society.
